en: The Eight Verses on the Consort of the Auspicious Lotus-Born One (Śrī-Kamalaja-Dayitāṣṭaka)
Composed by the venerable Śrī Śivābhinava Nṛsiṃha Bhāratī Svāmī:
[Salutations] to the Mother of Speech, whose lotus feet are served by sages such as Śuka on the mountain Śṛṅga,
and who dispels the chariot of the king of gods— the moon— with the shadow of her own body.
O beloved of the Lotus-born, while you are being joyfully worshipped by the hosts of the best of gods, headed by Śambhu and Śrīnātha, grant me quickly pure knowledge and wisdom. || 1 ||

At the beginning of the Kalpa, the Lord of Pārvatī, entreated by the preeminent hosts of gods and desiring to bring strength to the Vedic path, arrived at Mount Śṛṅgavat in the form of the best of ascetics;
having installed an image there, he performed worship with manifold prostrations— you who are she whose crest-jewel is the crescent moon.
O beloved of the Lotus-born, quickly grant me pure knowledge and wisdom. || 2 ||

O Beloved of the Lotus-born, having destroyed the flood of sins accumulated by many births, and having brought about a multitude of merits, please swiftly grant me faith, reverence for the words of the Vedas and the guru, firm devotion, and pure knowledge and intellect toward the assembly of gods, teachers, the twice-born, and all your own retinue. 3.

O Goddess, whose lotus-like hands shine with the vidyā, the mudrā, the rosary, and the jar of nectar; you who are expert in bestowing knowledge upon those who quickly bow down—even if they be dull-witted or deaf—having swiftly uprooted from within me the great natural enemies such as desire and the rest; [Please grant me the supreme state.]
O beloved of the Lotus-born, quickly grant me pure knowledge and wisdom. || 4 ||
O Goddess, ocean of mercy, having always granted me a most steadfast intellect regarding actions appropriate to my own self, strength of body for that purpose,
long life, fame renowned throughout the three worlds, detachment from the path of sin,
association with the virtuous, and even the hearing of sacred discourses— [grant these].
O beloved of the Lotus-born, quickly grant me pure knowledge and wisdom. || 5 ||

O Mother, your lotus feet have never been worshipped by me with various flowers out of devotion; I, dull-witted and indolent, am not even capable of singing your divine qualities in sublime verses. Yet, O Mother, as you did for your own child, you have bestowed incomparable compassion upon me, though I am mute and devoid of service.
O beloved of the lotus-born, grant me quickly pure knowledge and wisdom. || 6 ||
Bestow upon me the auspicious attainments of peace and the rest; quickly grant me that ever-distinct awakening, dispassion, and the longing for liberation while the glorious Śiva is being served.
O You whose lotus feet are worshipped by the hands of the foremost of yogis at the sacred ford of knowledge and elsewhere!
O beloved of the Lotus-born, grant me quickly pure knowledge and a purified intellect. || 7 ||

O Mother, having quickly accomplished hearing, reflection, and meditative absorption for me, whose nature is the Reality-consciousness, cause my inner mind to be constantly endowed with a longing for the non-conceptual Samādhi,
while I am seated upon the sovereign throne of the Cakra shining in the excellent palace that stands like a sprout upon the lofty bank.
O beloved of the Lotus-born, grant me quickly pure knowledge and wisdom. || 8 ||
Thus ends the Śrīkamalajadayitāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Śivābhinava Nṛsiṃhabhāratī Svāmī.
